source: NCERT Class XI, Themes in World History, Ch. 3 (Nomadic Empires).

sections.heading: 1. The Mongols and the Steppe
points: The chapter deals with the **Mongols**, a **nomadic pastoral** people of the Central Asian **steppes**.
Nomads herded animals (horses, sheep) and moved seasonally; they had no cities or agriculture but were skilled **horse-riders and archers**.
Nomadic society was organised into **clans and tribes**, sometimes forming confederations.

sections.heading: 2. Genghis Khan and the Mongol Empire
points: **Genghis Khan (Temujin)** united the warring Mongol tribes and was proclaimed **Great Khan in 1206** at an assembly (**quriltai**).
He built the **largest land empire** in history, stretching across Asia into Europe — through **military genius, discipline and organisation**.
The Mongol army was organised on the **decimal system (units of 10, 100, 1000, 10,000 = tumen)**; used speed, terror and effective siege tactics.
Conquests included **China, Central Asia, Iran, and parts of Russia and Europe**.

sections.heading: 3. Administration and the Yam
points: The Mongols set up an efficient administration over conquered lands, adopting local practices.
The **'yam'** — a fast **courier/postal relay system** — connected the vast empire.
They promoted **trade along the Silk Route**, ensuring safety of travellers (a period sometimes called the 'Pax Mongolica').
Mongol law was based on customary code (associated with the **yasa**).

sections.heading: 4. Nomads and Settled Societies
points: Relations between nomads and settled/agrarian societies were of both **conflict and exchange** (trade, tribute, plunder).
After Genghis Khan, the empire was divided among his sons into **uluses (khanates)**.
The Mongols were later **assimilated** into the cultures they conquered (e.g. adopting Islam, Chinese ways); their legacy shaped Eurasian history.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Genghis Khan (Temujin) proclaimed Great Khan in 1206 (at a quriltai).
Mongols = nomadic pastoralists of the Central Asian steppe; expert horse-archers.
Army organised on decimal system (tumen = 10,000).
The 'yam' = Mongol courier/postal relay system.
Empire divided into uluses (khanates) among Genghis Khan's sons.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Genghis Khan's original name was Temujin**; proclaimed Great Khan in **1206**.
The Mongol army used the **decimal (tens) system**; a **tumen = 10,000**.
The **'yam'** was a **courier/postal** relay system.
The Mongols built the **largest contiguous land empire** in history.
